description: Heelllo Boxcode support knowledge base — hand-authored Q&A entries used as grounding context for the chat assistant. Retrieval matches user messages against question, keywords, and category.

entries.question: What is Heelllo Boxcode?
entries.answer: Heelllo Boxcode is a platform for instant project scaffolding, live analytics, team workspaces, and one-click deploys. You can create a new project from a template in seconds and ship it without touching servers.

entries.question: How do I get started with my first project?
entries.answer: Sign up, open the dashboard, click New Project, pick a template (Next.js, Express, or static), and Boxcode scaffolds the repo for you. Then hit Deploy to publish it.

entries.question: What templates are available?
entries.answer: Boxcode ships templates for Next.js, Node/Express APIs, and static sites, with more on the way. Each includes sensible defaults like ESLint, TypeScript config, and a README.

entries.question: How long does it take to set up?
entries.answer: Under a minute. Sign up, scaffold a project, and deploy — the whole flow is designed to be done in one sitting.

entries.question: Do I need my own server or hosting?
entries.answer: No. One-click deploys handle hosting for your frontend. For custom needs you can point deployments at your own VPS or cloud account.

entries.question: Is there a demo or sample project?
entries.answer: The dashboard includes a sample analytics project you can explore without creating anything — open the left sidebar and click Sample Dashboard.

entries.question: What do I do after creating a project?
entries.answer: Clone it locally with git, run npm install and npm run dev, and start building. The README in each template walks through the exact commands.

entries.question: Can I import an existing codebase?
entries.answer: Yes — connect a GitHub repo from Project Settings → Import, or push your existing code to a new Boxcode project. Imports preserve your git history.

entries.question: What's the difference between a project and a workspace?
entries.answer: A project is one codebase (frontend, API, or static site). A workspace is a shared team container that groups projects, members, and billing.

entries.question: Where can I find documentation?
entries.answer: This assistant answers most questions, and each template ships with its own README. Full docs are linked from the dashboard footer.

entries.question: How do I sign up?
entries.answer: Click Sign Up on the login page and enter your name, email, and a password. Your account is created instantly and you're signed in with a JWT token.

entries.question: How do I log in?
entries.answer: Use the email and password you signed up with on the login page. Successful login returns a token that the dashboard stores and sends as a Bearer token.

entries.question: I forgot my password — how do I reset it?
entries.answer: Password reset isn't available yet. Contact support from the dashboard and we'll reset it manually for your account.

entries.question: Can I change my name or email?
entries.answer: Yes — go to Account Settings in the sidebar. Changing your email requires confirming the new address before it takes effect.

entries.question: How do I delete my account?
entries.answer: Account deletion is available in Account Settings → Danger Zone. It permanently removes your projects and chat history after a 7-day grace period.

entries.question: Can I have multiple accounts?
entries.answer: You can, but we recommend one account with multiple workspaces instead — billing and history stay cleaner in a single login.

entries.question: Why am I logged out suddenly?
entries.answer: Sessions last 7 days by default. You'll be logged out when the token expires, when the server's JWT_SECRET changes, or if you log in from a new device.

entries.question: How do I log out?
entries.answer: Use the Log Out button in the sidebar footer. Logging out clears the stored token from your browser.

entries.question: What happens to my data if I'm removed from a workspace?
entries.answer: Your personal account stays intact; you lose access to that workspace's projects and chat history. Re-invitation restores access.

entries.question: Can I use the same email for two workspaces?
entries.answer: Yes — your email identifies you across workspaces. You switch between them from the workspace switcher at the top of the sidebar.

entries.question: How much does Heelllo Boxcode cost?
entries.answer: There's a free plan for small teams. Paid plans start at $12 per seat per month and add unlimited projects, advanced analytics, and priority support.

entries.question: Is there a free trial?
entries.answer: The free plan is a permanent free tier, not a trial — no credit card required. Upgrade whenever you need more seats or analytics.

entries.question: What's included in the free plan?
entries.answer: The free plan includes one workspace, up to 3 projects, and 14 days of analytics history — enough for small teams to get started.

entries.question: What does the paid plan include?
entries.answer: Paid plans include unlimited projects, 12 months of analytics history, SSO-ready team permissions, and priority support. Billing is per seat per month.

entries.question: How does per-seat billing work?
entries.answer: You pay $12 per active member per month. Inactive members (no login for 90 days) don't count toward the bill.

entries.question: Can I change plans later?
entries.answer: Yes — upgrade or downgrade anytime from Billing settings. Changes are prorated to the end of the current billing cycle.

entries.question: Do you offer student or open-source discounts?
entries.answer: Yes — verified students and open-source maintainers get 50% off paid plans. Apply from Billing → Discounts with valid proof.

entries.question: What payment methods do you accept?
entries.answer: We accept all major credit and debit cards via Stripe. Invoicing for annual plans is available on request for teams.

entries.question: How do I get a refund?
entries.answer: Paid plans come with a 14-day money-back guarantee. Contact support from the dashboard and we'll process the refund to the original card.

entries.question: How do I create a new project?
entries.answer: Click New Project in the dashboard, pick a template, name it, and choose a workspace. Boxcode scaffolds the repo instantly.

entries.question: How do I delete a project?
entries.answer: Project Settings → Danger Zone → Delete Project. Deletion is permanent and also removes the deployed site after 24 hours.

entries.question: How do I rename a project?
entries.answer: Rename it from Project Settings. The URL slug updates too, and old links redirect for 30 days.

entries.question: Can I duplicate a project?
entries.answer: Yes — Project Settings → Duplicate creates a full copy including environment variables, but not your database contents.

entries.question: What is a project slug?
entries.answer: The slug is the short identifier in your project URL (e.g. my-app). It must be unique per workspace and can be edited in Project Settings.

entries.question: Where are environment variables configured?
entries.answer: Project Settings → Environment Variables. They're injected at build and runtime, and are never exposed to the browser unless prefixed NEXT_PUBLIC_.

entries.question: Can I use my own domain?
entries.answer: Yes — add a custom domain in Project Settings → Domains. We issue an SSL certificate automatically once DNS points at us.

entries.question: How do I invite a teammate to a project?
entries.answer: Project Settings → Members → Invite. Teammates must already have an account; you can assign Viewer or Editor roles.

entries.question: What happens when I archive a project?
entries.answer: Archiving pauses builds and deployments but keeps your code and history. Unarchive anytime from the project list.

entries.question: How do I see my projects?
entries.answer: All your projects are listed in the dashboard sidebar under your workspace. Use the search box to filter by name.

entries.question: How do I deploy my project?
entries.answer: Click Deploy in the project header. Boxcode builds and publishes to a preview URL first; promote it to production when you're happy.

entries.question: What platforms do you deploy to?
entries.answer: Frontends deploy to Vercel-compatible infrastructure, and the Express backend is designed for Render Web Services. Custom VPS/EC2 is supported for advanced users.

entries.question: How do I deploy the Express backend?
entries.answer: Push the repo, create a Render Web Service with root directory backend, build command npm install, start command node server.js, and set JWT_SECRET and CORS_ORIGIN.

entries.question: How do I deploy the Next.js frontend?
entries.answer: Connect the repo to Vercel, set the framework to Next.js, and add NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL pointing at your deployed backend. Vercel handles the build.

entries.question: What is a preview deployment?
entries.answer: Every push to a branch creates an isolated preview URL where you can test changes before they reach production. Preview URLs expire after 7 days.

entries.question: How do I set environment variables for production?
entries.answer: Add them in Project Settings → Environment Variables and redeploy. Values are encrypted at rest and only available at build/runtime on the server.

entries.question: My deploy failed — where do I start?
entries.answer: Open the deploy log from the Deployments tab. The most common causes are a failed npm install, a missing start script, or a syntax error in the build.

entries.question: How do I roll back a bad deployment?
entries.answer: Deployments tab → pick the last working deploy → Rollback. Rollbacks keep the old environment variables, so secrets aren't lost.

entries.question: Can I deploy from my local machine?
entries.answer: Yes — a CLI is coming to npm soon that will let you run deploy from the repo root. Until then, pushes to the main branch deploy automatically.

entries.question: How are domains and SSL handled?
entries.answer: Every deployment gets an https URL automatically. Custom domains get free SSL certs issued and renewed automatically.

entries.question: What analytics does Boxcode provide?
entries.answer: Live dashboards for page views, active users, events, and API usage — updated in near real time on the dashboard.

entries.question: How do I track a custom event?
entries.answer: Call our events API with an event name and optional properties: POST /api/events with your project token. Events appear in the dashboard within seconds.

entries.question: What is an active user?
entries.answer: An active user is a unique visitor with activity in the last 5 minutes. The dashboard shows active now and active today counts.

entries.question: How far back does analytics history go?
entries.answer: Free plans keep 14 days of history; paid plans keep 12 months. History is stored as aggregated daily buckets, not raw logs.

entries.question: Can I export analytics data?
entries.answer: Yes — export CSV or JSON from the analytics header. Exports include the current view's date range and filters.

entries.question: Why does my page view count look low?
entries.answer: Counts come from the snippet installed in your app. If the snippet loads late or is blocked by ad-blockers, views are undercounted.

entries.question: What is the analytics snippet?
entries.answer: A one-line script with your project token, added to the head of your site. It reports page views and referrers without cookies.

entries.question: Do you track individual users?
entries.answer: No — analytics are privacy-friendly and cookieless. We track aggregate events, never individual identities, so no consent banner is needed.

entries.question: Can I filter analytics by page or referrer?
entries.answer: Yes — the dashboard supports filters for page path, referrer, device, and country. Filters combine additively.

entries.question: How do I add analytics to my Next.js app?
entries.answer: Add the snippet to layout.tsx, or use the included Analytics component from the template. It reports route changes automatically on the client.

entries.question: How do I invite teammates?
entries.answer: Head to Team → Invite in the sidebar, enter their email addresses, and pick a role. They'll get an email with a join link.

entries.question: What roles exist?
entries.answer: Owner, Admin, Editor, and Viewer. Owners manage billing and deletion; Admins manage members; Editors can push code; Viewers can only read.

entries.question: How do I remove a teammate?
entries.answer: Team → Members → Remove. Removed members lose access immediately, and their personal data is retained on their own account.

entries.question: Can I change someone's role?
entries.answer: Yes — Team → Members → change role from the member's row. Owners can't be demoted by anyone but the owner.

entries.question: What is a workspace?
entries.answer: A workspace is your team's shared container for projects, members, and billing. One account can belong to many workspaces.

entries.question: How do I create a new workspace?
entries.answer: Workspace switcher → New Workspace. You become its owner and can invite members and create projects inside it.

entries.question: How do I switch between workspaces?
entries.answer: Use the workspace switcher at the top of the sidebar. Projects and analytics shown are always for the active workspace.

entries.question: Can a project belong to two workspaces?
entries.answer: No — each project lives in exactly one workspace. To share it, duplicate it into the other workspace or invite the people there as members.

entries.question: What happens to projects when I leave a workspace?
entries.answer: They stay with the workspace. If you created them, ownership transfers to an Admin; otherwise they're untouched.

entries.question: How do I transfer workspace ownership?
entries.answer: Team → Settings → Transfer Ownership. Only the current Owner can transfer, and the new owner must be an Admin.

entries.question: Is there a public API?
entries.answer: Yes — the backend exposes a REST API at /api. Auth endpoints are /api/auth/signup and /api/auth/login; everything else needs a Bearer token.

entries.question: How do I authenticate API requests?
entries.answer: Sign up or log in to get a JWT, then send it as Authorization: Bearer <token>. Tokens expire after 7 days.

entries.question: What does the chat API return?
entries.answer: POST /api/chat with { message } returns { reply } — the assistant's grounded answer — plus sources, the knowledge-base entries used as context.

entries.question: Are there rate limits?
entries.answer: Yes — 60 requests per minute per user on auth and chat endpoints. Exceeding it returns HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header.

entries.question: How do I report a bug in the API?
entries.answer: Include the request method, path, status code, and timestamp from the response headers. Support is reachable from the dashboard.

entries.question: What content type do requests use?
entries.answer: All request and response bodies are JSON (application/json). Send a Content-Type: application/json header on POST/PUT requests.

entries.question: What does the health endpoint do?
entries.answer: GET /health returns { status: 'ok' } and is used by load balancers and uptime monitors to check the API is alive.

entries.question: Can I call the API from a browser?
entries.answer: The API supports CORS for your configured origin, but browser calls expose your JWT. Server-side calls are safer for anything sensitive.

entries.question: How do I get the user's profile via API?
entries.answer: GET /api/auth/me with a Bearer token returns { name, email } for the authenticated user.

entries.question: What HTTP status codes should I handle?
entries.answer: 400 for bad input, 401 for missing/invalid token, 409 for duplicate signup, 429 for rate limits, and 5xx for server/provider errors. Your client should surface these gracefully.

entries.question: The dashboard shows Network Error — what now?
entries.answer: The frontend can't reach the API. Check that the backend is running on port 4000 and that NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL points at it.

entries.question: I get CORS errors in the browser console.
entries.answer: CORS blocks requests from origins not in the backend's CORS_ORIGIN setting. Set CORS_ORIGIN to your frontend URL (e.g. http://localhost:3000) and restart.

entries.question: Why do I get 401 Invalid or expired token?
entries.answer: The token is missing, expired (7 days), or the JWT_SECRET changed. Log out and log back in to mint a fresh token.

entries.question: The chat says 'LLM is not configured'.
entries.answer: That message means OPENAI_API_KEY isn't set in backend/.env. Add your key, restart the server, and try again.

entries.question: Chat returns 429 rate limited — why?
entries.answer: You exceeded 60 requests per minute on chat. Wait the seconds shown in the Retry-After header before trying again.

entries.question: npm install fails with better-sqlite3 build errors.
entries.answer: better-sqlite3 needs a native build. Install build tools (Xcode CLT on macOS, build-essential on Linux) or use Node 20+ which ships prebuilds.

entries.question: My question got an answer that sounds wrong.
entries.answer: The assistant only answers from the knowledge base. If the context didn't cover your question, it should say so — rephrase or ask about a covered topic like pricing or deployment.

entries.question: Where do I check server logs?
entries.answer: In development, the terminal running node server.js. On Render, the Logs tab of your Web Service. Logs include OpenAI call errors if something failed.

entries.question: The frontend builds but API calls 404.
entries.answer: The backend route path is wrong or the API is on a different port. Confirm the request goes to /api/... on port 4000 (or your deployed URL).

entries.question: How do I reset the local database?
entries.answer: Stop the server, delete backend/heelllo.db, and restart — tables are recreated automatically. This wipes users and chat history, so back up first.

entries.question: How are passwords stored?
entries.answer: Passwords are hashed with bcrypt (10 salt rounds) before being stored. Plaintext passwords are never kept or logged.

entries.question: How do JWTs work here?
entries.answer: Login/signup returns a JWT signed with your server's JWT_SECRET. The token carries the user id and expires after 7 days — keep JWT_SECRET long and random.

entries.question: Is my data encrypted at rest?
entries.answer: Yes — the SQLite database and deployed environment variables are encrypted at rest on our infrastructure.

entries.question: Should I commit .env files?
entries.answer: No. backend/.gitignore already excludes .env. Commit .env.example with placeholder values so teammates know which variables exist.

entries.question: What is JWT_SECRET and why does it matter?
entries.answer: It's the key that signs your auth tokens. If it leaks, anyone can forge tokens. Use a long random string and never share it.

entries.question: Can someone else see my API responses?
entries.answer: Traffic is HTTPS-only in production, so responses are encrypted in transit. Keep your Bearer tokens out of URLs and logs.

entries.question: How do I rotate JWT_SECRET safely?
entries.answer: Generate a new value, update the server, then ask users to log in again — old tokens are rejected after the change. Do it during low traffic.

entries.question: What does the API do with my chat messages?
entries.answer: Chat messages are stored in your workspace's SQLite database so your sidebar history persists between visits. Delete your account to remove them.

entries.question: Do you share data with third parties?
entries.answer: No — chat replies come from the local knowledge base, so no message data is sent to any third party or AI provider. Conversations are stored only in your workspace's SQLite database.

entries.question: What is Boxcode the assistant?
entries.answer: I'm the built-in support assistant for Heelllo Boxcode. I answer from the product's knowledge base, so my replies stay grounded in the docs.

entries.question: Is Boxcode the assistant an LLM?
entries.answer: No — I answer by matching your message against the local knowledge base and returning the best-matching entry's answer directly. No external AI or LLM calls are made.

entries.question: How does the assistant avoid hallucinating?
entries.answer: Every answer is looked up directly from the local knowledge base — the best-matching entry's answer is returned as-is, so there's nothing to invent.

entries.question: Where can I get human support?
entries.answer: Use the support form in the dashboard footer. Free plan replies within 3 business days; paid plans get priority support.

entries.question: What's on the roadmap?
entries.answer: Next up: a CLI, webhooks for deploy events, SSO for paid plans, and more project templates. Vote on features from the dashboard feedback tab.

entries.question: How do I give feedback?
entries.answer: The dashboard has a Feedback button in the footer. Feature votes and bug reports both go straight to the team.

entries.question: Is there a changelog?
entries.answer: Yes — the Changelog is linked in the dashboard footer and lists every release with bug fixes and new features.

entries.question: Who is behind Heelllo Boxcode?
entries.answer: Heelllo Boxcode is built by a small team focused on making the scaffold → deploy → analyze loop as fast as possible.

entries.question: How do I get enterprise support?
entries.answer: Enterprise plans include a dedicated support channel and SLAs. Contact sales from the dashboard footer to start a conversation.
